title: Total site of a coherent pseudofunctor of sites
statement: Let $I$ be a small category and let $(\mathcal C_i)_{i\in I}$ be sites [def-weil-size-convention] [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For every arrow $\alpha:i\to j$ suppose we have a continuous functor $u_\alpha:\mathcal C_j\to\mathcal C_i$, together with unit isomorphisms $u_{\mathrm{id}_i}\cong\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C_i}$ and compositor isomorphisms $u_\alpha u_\beta\cong u_{\beta\alpha}$ for composable $i\xrightarrow{\alpha}j\xrightarrow{\beta}k$, satisfying the unit and pentagon coherence laws. Assume that each $u_\alpha$ preserves the fibre products used to pull back covering families. The Grothendieck total category has objects $(i,U)$ with $U\in\mathcal C_i$ and arrows $(\alpha,f):(i,U)\to(j,V)$ for $\alpha:i\to j$, $U\in\mathcal C_i$, $V\in\mathcal C_j$, and $f:U\to u_\alpha(V)$ in $\mathcal C_i$; composition uses the compositor isomorphisms $u_\alpha u_\beta\cong u_{\beta\alpha}$ and is associative. The covering topology is generated by the vertical families $(\mathrm{id}_i,f_\ell):(i,U_\ell)\to(i,U)$ whose $f_\ell$ form a covering family in $\mathcal C_i$ (equivalently, a sieve is covering when it contains such a generating family). Pulling a generating cover back along any $(\alpha,f)$ is computed after applying $u_\alpha$ and forming the indicated pullback, and is again a covering, so this generated topology is a site and every isomorphism sieve is covering.

source.place: Tag 09WC, lemma-simplicial-site-site, Case A: total category, composition, and pullback stability of degreewise coverings; the identity/pentagon insert the canonical pseudofunctor coherence

proof.text: The objects and arrows are exactly the Grothendieck construction of the contravariant pseudofunctor: an arrow over $\alpha:i\to j$ is a map $U\to u_\alpha(V)$ in $\mathcal C_i$. Compose $(\alpha,f)$ with $(\beta,g)$ by applying $u_\alpha$ to $g$, composing with $f$, and inserting the compositor $u_\alpha u_\beta\cong u_{\beta\alpha}$. The unitors give identity arrows, and the assumed unit and pentagon coherence laws make the two composites of three arrows equal and make identities act as identities. Thus the displayed data form a category.

source.place: Tag 09WC, lemma-simplicial-site-site, Case A: objects, morphisms, composition; coherence is the unit and associativity check

proof.text: Declare the vertical families whose component maps form a covering in \mathcal C_i to be generating covers. Each fibre family is a covering by the site axioms in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and identity arrows are covers there. The topology generated by these families is the smallest Grothendieck topology containing them, so it has the identity, transitivity, and pullback-sieve axioms. Once the pullback stability is checked in Step 3, induction on the closure operations shows that a sieve is covering exactly when it contains one of the displayed vertical generating families (vertical refinements and composites remain in the generated closure).

source.place: Tag 09WC, lemma-simplicial-site-site, Case A: definition of covering families and the generated topology

proof.text: For an arrow $(\alpha,f):(i,U)\to(j,V)$ and a generating vertical cover $\{(\mathrm{id}_j,g_\ell):(j,V_\ell)\to(j,V)\}$, set $P_\ell=U\times_{u_\alpha(V)}u_\alpha(V_\ell)$ in $\mathcal C_i$, with projections $p_\ell:P_\ell\to U$ and $q_\ell:P_\ell\to u_\alpha(V_\ell)$. The arrows $(\mathrm{id}_i,p_\ell):(i,P_\ell)\to(i,U)$ and $(\alpha,q_\ell):(i,P_\ell)\to(j,V_\ell)$ form a commutative pullback square in the total category: commutativity is the equality $f p_\ell=u_\alpha(g_\ell)q_\ell$, and for any cone the equality of its two composites gives, after the compositor identification, a unique map to $P_\ell$ by the fibre-product universal property in $\mathcal C_i$; the same calculation with the unitors handles identities. Continuity of $u_\alpha$ says that $\{u_\alpha(g_\ell)\}$ is a covering and identifies the canonical comparison $u_\alpha(T\times_VV_\ell)\to u_\alpha(T)\times_{u_\alpha(V)}u_\alpha(V_\ell)$; the stated fibre-product-preservation hypothesis therefore identifies this $P_\ell$ with the pullback of the original vertical family. The site axiom in $\mathcal C_i$ makes $\{P_\ell\to U\}$ a covering. Thus generating covers are stable under pullback, and the generated topology is a site; its isomorphism sieves are covering by axiom (i) of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].
